proposal.utterance: How would you BFO-classify 'the capacity of an institution to repair itself'?

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity
entities.rationale: A capacity is paradigmatically a Disposition in BFO: it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (here, an institution), is internally grounded in the structural and functional properties of that bearer, and is realized when the institution actually undergoes self-repair processes. BFO_0000016 (Disposition) is the correct type because the capacity is grounded in intrinsic features of the institution (its rules, personnel, procedures) rather than being externally assigned. It is distinct from a Role (BFO_0000023), which is externally grounded. The capacity may or may not be exercised, but it persists as a feature of the institution.

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess
entities.rationale: The realization of the self-repair capacity is a Process (BFO_0000015): a temporal occurrent in which the institution modifies or corrects its own norms, structures, or practices. This class is needed to anchor the BFO_0000054 (realized in) relation from the disposition to its realization.

relations.rationale: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), the BFO category for internally-grounded capacities.

Self-repair capacity is plausibly a condition contributing to institutional legitimacy; LegalLegitimacyCondition already exists as a Disposition subclass, making InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity a natural specialization. Listed here as a candidate relation for user confirmation.
The self-repair capacity inheres in a LegalInstitution (its bearer), per the SDC-bearer relation RO_0000052 at the class level (domain-range constraint).
When exercised, the self-repair capacity is realized in an InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess, per BFO_0000054 (realized in).
InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess is a subclass of Process (BFO_0000015).

open_questions: Should InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity be a subclass of the existing LegalLegitimacyCondition (disposition), or should it be an independent disposition subclass directly under BFO_0000016? The subclass relation is proposed but may be too strong if self-repair is not always a legitimacy condition.

Is the bearer always a LegalInstitution, or could this capacity also inhere in other kinds of social institutions (e.g., non-legal normative systems)? This would affect whether the inheres-in domain should be LegalInstitution or a broader class.
Should InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess be linked to the existing InstitutionalPersistence (Quality) or InstitutionalEffectiveness (Quality) as a quality that is produced or enhanced by such processes?

Is 'capacity to repair itself' meant normatively (the institution ought to be able to repair) or descriptively (it in fact can)? This affects whether we prefer Disposition (descriptive, intrinsic) or a normative sub-type.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'capacity of an institution to repair itself' picks out an internally-grounded, specifically dependent continuant that inheres in an institution and is triggered under conditions of dysfunction or failure. In BFO 2020 this maps most precisely to Disposition (BFO_0000016): dispositions are grounded in intrinsic structural features of their bearers and are realized in processes. This is distinguished from a Role (externally conferred) or a Quality (a static measurable property). Two new classes are proposed: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity (Disposition) inhering in LegalInstitution, and InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess (Process) as its realization target. A candidate subclass relation to the existing LegalLegitimacyCondition is flagged for user confirmation, since whether self-repair is constitutive of legitimacy is a substantive theoretical commitment the user may or may not wish to endorse.
